question: On 26 February 2026, the European Court of Auditors concluded that more than half of the European Innovation Partnership projects for the agricultural sector did not yield any useful innovations, and around a third had little relevance to agricultural practice. Unlike researchers and advisers, farmers were not systematically compensated for their participation. Projects that do compensate farmers, such as those in the Netherlands, demonstrably perform better. 1.

Is the Commission prepared to set a minimum percentage, in the regulation governing the programme for the 2028–2034 period, for European Innovation Partnership projects that must demonstrably prove to be applicable in agricultural practice?

The Commission promises to strengthen the interactive innovation approach – the same promise it made at the start of the current programme period. What, specifically, is it doing differently compared to 2021?

Can the Commission specify a concrete, quantifiable target for farmer participation that it aims to achieve for the European Innovation Partnership in the 2028–2034 period, against which Parliament can hold it to account halfway through that period?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (18.6.2026) The Commission welcomes the European Court of Auditor’s special report1 and remains committed to further refining the measure for Operational Groups (OG) projects. The Commission will not propose minimum percentage targets for projects since this would conflict with the bottom-up approach of the measure.

The Commission is committed to improve the focus on farmers’ innovation needs in OG projects, as recommended by the Court. Under the Common Agricultural Policy (CAP) 2023-2027, the interactive innovation model became a legal requirement, whereas it was non-binding guidance during the CAP 2014-2022 (the period covered by the audit).

In its legal proposal for the CAP 2028-2034, in line with the recommendations by the Court, the Commission has proposed: emphasis on the dissemination of key results and scaling-up of project outcomes, strengthening the interactive innovation model to ensure that farmers and other practitioners are actively involved in projects and proposing a new possibility for Member States to support specific actions aimed at the wider uptake of OG projects’ results.

The Commission will aim to also continue supporting EIPAGRI2 under Horizon Europe 2028-2034 via the multi-actor approach, addressed in the upcoming strategic approach to Research and Innovation. OG projects must bring together partners with complementary expertise, while ensuring the active involvement of farmers and other relevant practitioners.

Fixed targets are not in line with the bottom-up nature of the measure and would hinder projects in for example forestry or rural innovation. Nevertheless, the Commission encourages and already observes improved farmers’ participation, with an increase of around 30% to 40% compared to the previous period.
1 https://www.eca.europa.eu/en/publications?ref=sr-2026-09. 2 EIP-AGRI: European Innovation Partnership for agricultural productivity and sustainability.
